concepts.title: Magnetic Field and Field Lines
concepts.definition: The space surrounding a magnet where its magnetic force can be detected by other magnets or magnetic materials.
concepts.key_idea: Field lines form continuous loops from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet.
question_patterns: What are the characteristics of magnetic field lines?
Why do magnetic field lines never cross each other?
Describe the direction of magnetic field lines inside and outside a magnet.
How is the strength of a magnetic field represented visually?

solution_steps.explain: Field lines emerge from the North pole and enter the South pole externally.
Lines never intersect because a compass cannot point in two directions at once.
Closer lines indicate a stronger magnetic field.

concepts.title: Magnetic Field of a Straight Conductor
concepts.definition: In brief, the magnetic field formed by a straight current-carrying wire is made up of concentric circular lines centered on the wire.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Field strength varies in direct proportion with current and in inverse proportion with the distance from the wire.
question_patterns: How does the magnetic field change if the current in a straight wire increases?
What is the pattern of field lines around a straight conductor?
Calculate the relative change in field if distance from the wire is doubled.
Describe the relationship between current and magnetic field magnitude.

solution_steps.explain: The field strength is calculated as the ratio of current to distance.

concepts.title: Right-Hand Thumb Rule
concepts.definition: In brief, a rule used to determine the magnetic's direction field around a current-holding conductor.
concepts.key_idea: Thumb points to current; curled fingers show the direction of magnetic field lines.
question_patterns: State the Right-Hand Thumb Rule.
Find the direction of the magnetic field for a vertical wire with upward current.
Apply Maxwell's corkscrew rule to a conductor.
What is the field direction below a horizontal wire carrying current from East to West?

solution_steps.explain: Point the right thumb in the direction of the electric current.
The direction in which the fingers wrap around the conductor is the direction of the magnetic field.

concepts.title: Magnetic Field of a Circular Loop
concepts.definition: In brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the magnetic field formed by a circular wire loop where field lines become straight at the center.
concepts.key_idea: The total field strength increases linearly with the turn count in the coil.
question_patterns: Why does a coil with multiple turns produce a stronger magnetic field?
Describe the field lines at the center of a circular loop.
Calculate the total field for a coil with n turns.
How does the direction of current in a loop affect the field at the center?

solution_steps.explain: Since current in each turn flows in the same direction, fields add up.

concepts.title: Magnetic Field in a Solenoid
concepts.definition: A cylindrical coil of many insulated copper wire turns that produces a uniform magnetic field inside when current flows.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, the internal magnetic field of a solenoid is uniform and parallel.
question_patterns: What is a solenoid?
Describe the nature of the magnetic field inside a current-carrying solenoid.
Compare the magnetic field of a solenoid with a bar magnet.
How can a solenoid be used to make an electromagnet?

solution_steps.explain: Inside the solenoid, field lines are parallel straight lines, indicating a uniform field.
One end acts as a North pole and the other as a South pole, similar to a bar magnet.

concepts.title: Force on a Conductor in a Magnetic Field
concepts.definition: In brief, the mechanical force felt by a current-carrying wire when placed inside an external magnetic field.
concepts.key_idea: Force is maximum when the current direction is perpendicular to the magnetic field direction.
question_patterns: When is the force on a conductor in a magnetic field the largest?
What happens to the force if the current direction is reversed?
Describe the effect of a magnetic field on a moving electron.
How does the strength of the magnet affect the displacement of a rod?

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the current and magnetic field are perpendicular for maximum force.
Use Fleming's Left-Hand Rule to find the direction of the resulting force.

concepts.title: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, a rule to find the direction of force using the thumb (motion), forefinger (field), and middle finger (current) of the left hand.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, the three parameters—Force, Field, and Current—are mutually perpendicular.
question_patterns: State Fleming's Left-Hand Rule.
An electron moves East in a Northward magnetic field; find the force direction.
Which finger represents the magnetic field in Fleming's rule?
Determine the direction of motion of a proton in a magnetic field.

solution_steps.explain: Point the forefinger in the direction of the magnetic field.
Point the middle finger in the direction of the current (opposite to electron flow).
The thumb points in the direction of the force or motion.

concepts.title: Domestic Electric Circuits
concepts.definition: The system of wiring used in homes, typically involving live, neutral, and earth wires at a potential of 220V.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Appliances are joined in parallel to ensure they receive the same voltage.
question_patterns: What are the colors of live, neutral, and earth wires?
What is the potential difference in Indian domestic circuits?
Why are domestic appliances connected in parallel?
Explain the function of the earth wire.

solution_steps.explain: Live (red) carries current, Neutral (black) completes the circuit, Earth (green) provides safety.
The standard potential difference between live and neutral is 220 V.

concepts.title: Short Circuit and Overloading
concepts.definition: Conditions of excessive current flow brought about by direct contact of live and neutral wires or connecting too many appliances.
concepts.key_idea: Fuses protect circuits by melting when current exceeds a safe limit.
question_patterns: What causes a short circuit?
Define overloading in an electric circuit.
How does a fuse prevent damage during a short circuit?
What happens to the current during a short circuit?

solution_steps.explain: Direct contact between live and neutral wires leads to a sudden current surge.
The high current produces heat that melts the fuse wire, breaking the circuit.

concepts.title: Domestic Power Safety Calculation
concepts.definition: In brief, Calculating the current drawn by an appliance to work out if it exceeds the circuit's safety rating.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, If the current drawn exceeds the fuse rating, the fuse will blow.
question_patterns: An appliance of 2kW is used in a 220V circuit with a 5A fuse. Will the fuse blow?
Calculate the current drawn by a 1.1kW electric iron.
What power rating can a 5A circuit support at 220V?
Determine if a circuit is overloaded given appliance power and fuse limit.

solution_steps.explain: Power in kilowatts must be multiplied by 1000.
Current is the power in watts divided by the voltage.
Check if current_drawn is greater than the fuse_limit.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A current through a horizontal power line flows in {direction} direction. What is the direction of magnetic field at a point directly below it?

solution_template.explain: Point thumb towards West. Fingers wrap in a clockwise direction when viewed from the East.
At a point below the wire, the field direction is towards the North (or clockwise in the perpendicular plane).

worked_examples.question_pattern: An electron enters a magnetic field at right angles to it. The direction of force acting on the electron will be?

solution_template.explain: Current direction is opposite to electron motion.
Forefinger in field direction, middle finger opposite to electron motion; thumb points into the page.
